Apple yesterday released the fifth beta of iOS 27, which includes changes such as new app icons and design adjustments to Spotlight search. It turns out that this update also contains code references to all new iPhone models expected to launch in the next six to eight months.

References to Unreleased iPhone Models

According to Macworld, which first spotted it, the fifth beta of iOS 27 contains internal references to six unreleased iPhones, covering the entire iPhone 18 lineup, the iPhone Air 2, and the upcoming foldable iPhone Ultra. These code references were found in "system files related to iPhone battery drivers and Battery Intelligence features."

The code only contains Apple internal identifiers (such as V62, V63, etc.) and does not list marketing names. However, based on other leaks, these model identifiers can be mapped to their expected marketing names:

  • V62: iPhone Air 2
  • V63: iPhone 18 Pro
  • V64: iPhone 18 Pro Max
  • V67: iPhone 18
  • V68: iPhone Ultra (or iPhone Fold)
  • V69: iPhone 18e

This update does not contain any further information about these devices. Apple is expected to kick off the iPhone 18 cycle next month with the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. The iPhone Ultra is also expected to be unveiled next month.

The iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and iPhone Air 2 are reportedly set to launch sometime in early 2027. This is the first year Apple has reshuffled the iPhone release schedule, splitting new device launches into two windows throughout the year.
